text: 44-year-old male. The patient's daughter reports a 1-week history of right leg weakness, unsteady gait, and multiple falls. Over the past 6 months, the patient has been increasingly forgetful, losing his way on familiar routes and facing difficulties operating simple kitchen appliances. He has also been paranoid, agitated, and restless recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to undiagnosed HIV/AIDS.

The rapid progression of neurological deficits over one week combined with the MRI findings of disseminated, non-enhancing white matter lesions is highly characteristic of PML, which is caused by the JC virus reactivation in immunocompromised individuals. We must immediately test for HIV and CD4 count to confirm the underlying immune status.
